requirement: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The code marked {impl} covers every obligation, and the tests cover the code-driven obligations. The only gap in the tests is the stylesheet rules, explained below.

**Implementation**
- `shield_badge` (src/lib.rs:444) builds a static `img.shields.io/badge/<label>-<message>-<color>` image. Its alt text is `"<label> <message>"`, which gives the role (or kind) and the full name. The URL and the alt text are escaped, which is covered separately by `safe_badges`.
- `replace_references` (src/lib.rs:384) renders each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` reference as `<a class="habeas-req-badge habeas-req-ref-<kind>" href=…>` around a shield image.
  - The link target is built by `chapter_href` from the current chapter path to the target's chapter path, plus the anchor `habeas-<req|example>-<name>`. The anchor comes from `DefinitionKind::anchor` (src/lib.rs:82). Relative `../` prefixes make links work from nested chapters.
  - References that fail validation, or that name no known definition, are left as literal text.
  - `ReferenceKind::label` and `ReferenceKind::color` give each role its text and colour.
- `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:285) renders each valid, closed fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive as a shield image. The image kind comes from `DefinitionKind::badge` ("req" or "example"). The image sits inside an element with the anchor id. Text outside directives is copied through unchanged. Directives with invalid names stay literal.
- `md/habeas.css` is anchored as an {impl}:
  - `a.habeas-req-badge:visited` keeps `color: inherit` with no decoration, so badges look the same whether or not visited. The badge text is inside the image anyway.
  - `a.habeas-req-badge:focus-visible` draws a 2px outline, which is the required keyboard-focus indicator.
  - `a.habeas-req-badge:hover` applies `brightness(1.08)`, the optional hover brightening.
  - The stylesheet is shipped to user projects through `BADGE_CSS` in setup.rs and wired in by `book.toml`.
- Everything the code does is covered by this requirement or by definitions it also cites. Examples are the "See evidence" link and the detail-page link, which `index.navigation` specifies, and escaping, which `safe_badges` specifies. The `{impl}` markings on the relevant functions are complete.

**Tests**
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` checks the Shields URL structure and the alt text, `"req requirements.foo_bar-baz"`.
- `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` renders `impl`, `cite` and `test` references from `guides/deep.md`. It asserts the badge class, the cross-chapter href `../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.ready`, and the per-role colour in the Shields URL. It also checks that the definition anchor exists in the defining chapter.
- `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` checks that a fenced `:::{req}` becomes a badge and that an inline `{req}` role outside a directive stays literal.
- `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` covers example definition badges (alt text `"example requirements.something.foo"`). It checks that a `{test}` link to an example works from a nested chapter. It also checks that an invalid example name and an example inside a code fence stay literal.
- `chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name` and `chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book` add checks on definition badge alt text and on invalid references staying literal.

**Gap:** the CSS rules for visited legibility, keyboard focus and hover have no automated test. They are small declarative rules whose real effect is visual and browser-dependent, and the badge text is inside the image. I judge that absence acceptable, though a simple string assertion on the stylesheet would be easy to add.

text: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
